- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- If model shows gradual upward trend with no spike, but true outcome spikes sharply, reduce forecast slope to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overcorrects downward; apply slight upward bias to prevent premature mean reversion.
- When official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% downward adjustment.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misread momentum; use moving average of last 5 sentiment values to smooth forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from forecast mean, check if recent auction events (especially CAP3/EU) caused supply shock; adjust for event-driven volatility.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often underestimates volatility; increase forecast standard deviation by 10–20% for hedging.
- When official event count is high and supply net is negative, model tends to over-predict recovery; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next period.
